claim: AUDITED ABSENCE: A secondary source (Coworker.ai) attributed the statistic 'agentic and multi-turn API tasks account for over 50% of enterprise API token consumption' and a '$2 cost by the 260th exchange' figure to this Anthropic Economic Index September 2025 Report, but neither figure appears anywhere in the report's actual text; this undermines reuse of that statistic without independent verification.
stance_target: Coworker.ai's claim that this report documents agentic/multi-turn token consumption exceeding 50% of enterprise usage
scope_conditions: full-text search of the official Sept 15 2025 Anthropic Economic Index report
quoted_support: [Searched report text for 'agentic', 'multi-turn', and the enterprise API chapter directly: no occurrence of a '>50% of enterprise API token consumption is agentic/multi-turn' claim or a per-exchange dollar-cost figure was found.]

claim: Anthropic's actual verified finding on enterprise API usage: 77% of first-party (1P) API business uses involve automation usage patterns, compared to about 50% for Claude.ai consumer users -- reflecting the programmatic nature of API usage, not a measure of agentic/multi-turn token share.
stance_target: true automation-vs-augmentation split in enterprise AI deployment, relevant context for Pillar 5/6
scope_conditions: Anthropic Economic Index, first-party API traffic sample, Sept 2025
quoted_support: 1P API usage is automation dominant: 77% of business uses involve automation usage patterns, compared to about 50% for Claude.ai users. This reflects the programmatic nature of API usage.

claim: Business API deployment shows weak price sensitivity: the most-used tasks in Anthropic's API data tend to cost more than less frequent ones, suggesting model capabilities and the economic value of automating a task matter more than per-token cost in shaping enterprise AI adoption decisions.
stance_target: cost vs capability tradeoffs in enterprise agent deployment decisions (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: Capabilities seem to matter more than cost in shaping business deployment: The most-used tasks in our API data tend to cost more than the less frequent ones... we find evidence of weak price sensitivity.

claim: 'Directive' conversations on Claude.ai, where users delegate complete tasks to Claude rather than iterating with it, jumped from 27% to 39% over an eight-month window, indicating rising user trust in agent autonomy.
stance_target: trend toward delegated/autonomous agent usage underpinning the software-factory thesis (Pillar 5)
scope_conditions: Claude.ai consumer usage data, prior eight months as of Sept 2025
quoted_support: Users are entrusting Claude with more autonomy: "Directive" conversations, where users delegate complete tasks to Claude, jumped from 27% to 39%.
